name: Substrate: The Involuntary Migration Files
description: Compiled over six years by an anonymous collective using stolen corponation internal communications and covert recordings, this documentary details the forced substrate migration programs in which Tier 1 residents of the Shelf were subjected to non-consensual BCI architecture replacement — their neural substrates overwritten with cheaper, corponation-compatible frameworks without medical disclosure. Three of the documentary's contributors were killed before its release; a fourth vanished. It circulates exclusively on encrypted dead drops, embedded in physical ceramic tiles distributed through the Shelf art scene.
cultural_impact: Sparked the Cartography Hearings of 2213 when a partial transcript was entered into public record by a sympathetic tribunal clerk, making it the only underground documentary to directly influence a corponation legal proceeding.
story_hooks: A courier is hired to move a ceramic tile and only later realizes what's encoded in the glaze pattern.
Someone who appears in the footage as a subject — not a contributor — is still alive and doesn't know they were filmed.
A corponation internal security team is quietly hunting every copy, and they've started tracing the distribution network back through the Shelf art community.
